Notice Inviting Tender (NIT)

University of Hyderabad (herein after referred to as UoH) invites sealed tenders under Two Bid
System (Technical bid and Price bid) from reputed, authorized distributors / wholesale & retail local
chemists to enter into Rate Contract for supply of branded Allopathic Medicines which are used in
the treatment of chronic ailments / diseases for Health Centre, University of Hyderabad.

The Tender Document can be downloaded free of cost from the University website
(www.uohyd.ac.in/tenders) and the Central Public Procurement (CPP) Portal
(https://eprocure.gov.in).

The Tenderer shall submit the Technical Bid and Price Bid separately in sealed envelopes,
clearly superscribed as:

e °“TECHNICAL BID FOR SUPPLY OF ALLOPATHIC MEDICINES TO UoH”
e “PRICE BID FOR SUPPLY OF ALLOPATHIC MEDICINES TO UoH”
Both envelopes shall be placed in one sealed outer envelope superscribed as:
“TENDER FOR SUPPLY OF ALLOPATHIC MEDICINES TO UoH”

The tender shall be addressed to:

The Assistant Registrar
Central Procurement Unit,

Room No. 122, Ground Floor
Administrative Building
University of Hyderabad
Hyderabad — 500046, Telangana.

The completed Tender Documents shall be submitted on or before 30.10.2026 up to 3:00
P.M. The sealed tenders shall be deposited in the Tender Box kept for the purpose at Room No. 122,
Central Procurement Unit, Administrative Building, University of Hyderabad, Hyderabad — 500046.

No bid shall be accepted after the stipulated date and time. The University shall not be responsible
for any delay in delivery of the tender documents due to postal, courier or any other reasons.

The Price Bids of only those bidders who are found technically qualified upon scrutiny of the
Technical Bids shall be opened subsequently. The date, time and venue for opening of the Price Bids shall
be intimated separately to the technically qualified bidders if required.

The University of Hyderabad reserves the right to accept or reject any or all bids, in whole or in
part, without assigning any reason thereof. The University also reserves the right to cancel, withdraw,
modify or terminate the tender process at any stage without assigning any reason.

In the event of cancellation of the tender process, the EMD, wherever applicable, shall be returned
to the respective bidders without any interest, in accordance with the applicable rules and terms and
conditions of the Tender Document. ,

The University of Hyderabad (UoH) proposes to enter into a Rate Contract with reputed and eligible
authorized distributors / wholesale and retail local chemists, fulfilling the prescribed eligibility criteria, for
the supply of branded Allopathic Medicines, preferably Equivalent Generic Drugs/Medicines, required for
use in the Health Centre, University of Hyderabad.

The tenure of the Rate Contract shall be for a period of Two (02) years, subject to satisfactory
performance, which shall be reviewed on a quarterly basis.

Authorized distributors and wholesale/retail local chemists having a minimum annual turnover of
%2.50 Crores in the supply of Allopathic Medicines/Generic Drugs during the last four financial years ending
31 March 2026 shall be eligible to participate in the Tender. The other eligibility criteria and requirements
are specified in the Terms and Conditions of the Tender (Annexure-I).

Agencies intending to participate in the Rate Contract shall carefully examine the Tender Document
and ensure that they fulfil all the eligibility criteria and requirements prescribed by the University. Bids
submitted by agencies not fulfilling the prescribed eligibility criteria are liable to be rejected.

The Rate Contract shall be governed by the Terms and Conditions enclosed with this Tender
Enquiry as Annexure-I. The bidders shall carefully examine all the terms and conditions before submitting
their bids. No modification, alteration or conditional acceptance of the prescribed terms and conditions
shall be entertained. Accordingly, bidders are advised to submit their bids only if they accept the terms
and conditions of the Tender Document in their entirety and fulfil all the prescribed eligibility criteria.

The bidders shall furnish Bid Security of %7,50,000/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Fifty Thousand only)
along with their Technical Bid in the form of an Account Payee Demand Draft, Fixed Deposit Receipt,
Banker's Cheque or Bank Guarantee drawn on any Commercial Bank, in favour of “Finance Officer,
University of Hyderabad” Payable at Hyderabad. Where the Bid Security is furnished in the form of a Fixed
Deposit Receipt (FDR) / Bank Guarantee (BG) and shall remain valid for a period of 165 days from the date
of opening of the Technical Bids.

The Bid Security shall be liable for forfeiture in accordance with the applicable rules and the terms
and conditions of the Tender Document, including in the event of withdrawal of the bid by the bidder
before expiry of the prescribed bid validity period of 120 days.

Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) registered under the applicable MSME provisions and holding
a valid NSIC Certificate under the Single Point Registration Scheme (SPRS) shall be exempted from payment

of EMD/Bid Security, subject to submission of valid documentary proof/certificate establishing their
eligibility for such exemption.

The estimated value of medicines proposed to be procured/supplied under the Rate Contract is
approximately in the range of %9.50 lakh to 10.00 lakh per month.

ANNEXURE-I

TERMS AND CONDITIONS FOR RATE CONTRACT
FOR SUPPLY OF ALLOPATHIC MEDICINES

This tender enquiry is for the purpose of executing Rate contract for supply of allopathic lifesaving
medicines for the treatment of hypertension, coronary artery disease, diabetes, Asthma,

cerebrovascular accident, epilepsy, psychosis, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder & depression which are
used in Health Centre, University of Hyderabad, Hyderabad.

The vendor must have access to ensure proper storage and to maintain require temperature during
transport of medicines until it reaches to Health Centre of University of Hyderabad

The successful bidder shall supply and distribute the Branded Medicines, on daily basis to the
beneficiaries listed in the Health Card issued by the University of Hyderabad as per the indents issued
by the Doctors of the Health Centre of University of Hyderabad once in a month only to the eligible
employees and dependents. The average number of prescriptions per day may range between 30 and
40 and types of medicines to be delivered per day would be in range of 350-400. Indents are based on
prescriptions from Health Centre Doctors / Doctors from University recognized hospitals.

The value of medicines to be supplied would approximately be in the range of Rs.9.5 Lakh to Rs.10
Lakh per month.

The vendor shall commence supply and distribution of the branded “admissible lifesaving medicines”
which are generally prescribed for chronic ailments from the day awarding the contract and the vendor
should ensure that sufficient stock of such medicines is kept in the Pharmacy.

The vendor should complete the supply and delivery of medicines on the next working day (within 20
hours i.e. collection of prescription by 4.00 PM, supply of medicines next morning (next working day)
latest by 12.00 Noon) of issue of prescriptions and at one go only (not in piece meal). Failure to deliver
the medicines within the stipulated time would entail levy of penalty. Substitute medicines should not
be supplied without the written approval of Chief Medical Officer (CMO)/Medical Officer (MO).

The vendor shall arrange the following man-power for collection of prescription from Health Centre and
supply of medicines to the patients / attendants of the patient:

a) 1 (one) qualified Pharmacist having thorough knowledge of medicines

b) 2 (two) helpers/Attendants for supply and distribution of medicines.

The pharmacist and supporting staff of vendor should be present from 10.00 a.m to 04.00 p.m at
University Health Centre on all working days.

The location of Pharmacy is at University of Hyderabad Health Centre. The vendor will be provided
adequate space free of charge within the premises of Health Centre with lock and key facility to store
the medicines. The vendor should have his own Refrigerator at Pharmacy. The Vendor should arrange
Personal Computer with printer and appropriate software so that the data, such as patient ID, patient
name and medicines supplied can be entered into and accessed whenever required. The data should
be shared online with the office of CMO and office of Finance officer. The University will provide
necessary logistics support in installing this facility and will also provide LAN internet facility. The cost
of establishment including salaries for this purpose shall be borne by the Vendor.

At the time of delivery of medicines, the vendor should generate invoice (in triplicate) against each

indent. The vendor shall obtain acknowledgement of the patient / attendant on the reverse side of the
invoice and the indent.

The vendor should submit the invoices along with a computer-generated consolidated statement (in
triplicate) to the Chief Medical Officer & in-charge Health Centre once in every 15 days for processing
of payment. The bill so submitted will be settled within one month in consultation with finance
thereafter. The fortnightly bill should contain the full details with regard to the date, ID No. and name
of the employee, name of medicines, description and quantity of medicines supplied, Manufacturing
Date, Batch No and Expiry date, MRP, discount and net price of each of the medicine and the total

your loved parents and siblings when engaging in any activities related to substance abuse.

prohibited substances is strictly prohibited on our campus. This is in accordance with the Narcotic Drugs
and Psychotropic Substances Act of 1985 (NDPS Act), enacted by the Government of India.

I urge all students to take this matter seriously and avoid any direct or indirect involvement with drug use
or the encouragement of such behavior. Your cooperation is essential in maintaining a drug-free campus
and fostering a safe and peaceful environment for everyone.

Item No.AC:95:2025:04: Report on admissions to the Ph.D. Programmes for the Academic
Year 2024-25.

The report presented by the Controller of Examinations on admission to the Ph.D. programmes for the
Academic Year 2024-25 was noted by the Council. The Council noted that an admission notification
for all the Ph.D. programmes for Academic Year 2025-26 has been released by the Office of the
Controller of Examinations and that the 22 academic units have opted to offer admission based on the
Entrance Exam to be held by the University and 20 academic units have decided to grant admissions
based on the UGC NET/ CSIR NET scores.

Chairman informed the House that the admissions to the Ph.D. programmes for last academic year
was held in two different modes, that is, by conducting the entrance exam and based on the scores of
UGC NET/CSIR NET as per the options exercised by the academic unit concerned. The admissions
to these programmes were concluded by conducting admission counselling and operation of wait list
and the process of admissions was formally closed in the month of February, 2025. At the end 109
seats in total remained unfilled. Out of which 17 seats for the streams for which entrance exams were
held and 92 seats against the NET based admission mode. It was also informed to the House that about
fifty percent of vacant seats were meant for reserved categories. The chief reason for said percentage
of reserved seats being vacant was on account of the fact that the candidates belonging to these
categories were admitted against the un-reserved category and hence there were no takers the seats

meant for them.

Keeping the above experience in view, the Chairman requested all the academic units to pay serious
attention towards the above phenomenon and to choose the admission mode carefully which can draw
a healthy competition and help the University fill all the seats. Accordingly, the Chairman advised all
the unit Heads to rework on it and to communicate their decision to the Controller of Examinations to
effect necessary changes in the admission notification for 2025-26 by bringing suitable amendments.
The House agreed to allow time for the academic units to act upon the above suggestion of the
Chairman and to communicate their decision to the CE latest by 2 May 2025.

The Council noted that the results of UGC-CSIR NET exam held in the month of January 2025 are
yet to be out and thus the candidates aspiring for admission into the University of Hyderabad will be
at disadvantage if the last date for submission of applications is not extended beyond 5 May 2025 for
the programmes for which NET scores are considered. Accordingly, it was resolved to extend the last
date for submission of application for NET based admissions up to 30 May 2025 and to include ICMR
JRF to be eligible for Ph.D. programmes in School of Life Sciences.

The Council noted that as per the guidelines issued by the UGC during March 2024, the candidates
awarded JRF shall be selected based on the performance in the interview out of 30 marks. Whereas,
the selection of category 2 & 3 of NET qualified candidates are based on combined marks scored by
them in the NET and the interview. The members felt that this situation is likely to put the Non-JRF
candidates to the disadvantage. Hence, the Council resolved that an Admission Committee may be
constituted to find out possible ways and means of appropriating the seats to the Non-JRF (category
2 & 3 of NET scores) candidates also, in accordance with UGC guidelines.
